plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of fragrant flowers. It is widely cultivated in gardens and in large fields for its essential oil, and it attracts bees and butterflies in great numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to late summer, peaking in late June and July
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the Romans added it to their bathwater, which is the origin of its name from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Tilia cordata
plants.description: A large deciduous tree with heart-shaped leaves that produces clusters of small, intensely fragrant, creamy-yellow flowers hanging from a distinctive leafy bract. The blossoms fill the air with a honey-like scent and are a major nectar source for bees.
plants.location: Europe and western Asia, commonly planted along streets and in parks across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Linden blossom is dried to make a calming herbal tea, and linden honey is among the most prized varieties in Europe.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: A aquatic perennial with large round floating leaves and showy, star-shaped white flowers that open in the morning and close in the afternoon. It grows in still or slow-moving freshwater lakes and ponds.
plants.location: Lakes and ponds across Europe, North Africa, and parts of western Asia
plants.funFact: The flower stalks of water lilies lengthen or shorten to keep the blossoms at the water surface, even as water levels change, and the seeds ripen underwater after the flower stalk coils down.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with large rounded clusters of showy flowers. Blossoms may be pink, blue, or purple depending on soil conditions, and the plant thrives in partial shade with moist soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early autumn, beginning in June in temperate regions
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in gardens in Europe, North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Soil acidity determines flower color: acidic soil with available aluminum yields blue blooms, while neutral to alkaline soil produces pink ones.
